questions.title: Leap Year Checker
questions.description:
Every February 29 the calendar team re-checks the leap year rule: a year is leap if it is divisible by 400, or divisible by 4 but not by 100. Decide using the logical operators || and &&.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer year.

Output Format:
Print a single line, lowercase true or false.

Constraints:
1 <= year <= 3000.

questions.title: Permission Flags Checker
questions.description:
A server stores user rights as an 8-bit permission mask. Given two users' masks, report the rights they share, the rights anyone holds, and the rights only the first user has. Use the bitwise operators & and | (with ~ for the complement).

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers p1 and p2.

Output Format:
Print three lines: 'Shared: X' where X = p1 & p2, then 'Combined: Y' where Y = p1 | p2, then 'Only in first: Z' where Z = p1 & ~p2.

Constraints:
0 <= p1, p2 <= 255.

questions.title: Grade From Marks Ternary Chain
questions.description:
An exam portal maps marks to letter grades with a single nested ternary expression (if statements are forbidden): 90 or above is A, 75 to 89 is B, 60 to 74 is C, 40 to 59 is D, below 40 is F.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer marks.

Output Format:
Print the single letter grade.

Constraints:
0 <= marks <= 100.

questions.title: Meter to Feet and Inches Converter
questions.description:
A travel app converts metres for hikers. It reports the complete feet (truncated with an explicit (int) cast) plus the leftover inches, using 1 metre = 3.28084 feet.

Input Format:
One line with a single decimal number meters.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Feet: N' where N is the integer part of meters * 3.28084 obtained by an (int) cast. Line 2: 'Inches: X' where X is the remaining (totalFeet - feet) * 12 printed to exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= meters <= 100.

questions.title: XOR Swap Without Extra Variable
questions.description:
Old-school programmers swapped two variables without any extra variable using only the XOR operator. Demonstrate the trick: apply a ^= b, then b ^= a, then a ^= b.

Input Format:
One line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print two lines after the swap: 'First: X' holding the original b, then 'Second: Y' holding the original a.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 100000.

questions.title: Electricity Bill Slab Calculator
questions.description:
A city bills electricity in slabs: the first 100 units cost 3.50 per unit, the next 100 units cost 5.00 per unit, and every unit above 200 costs 8.00 per unit. Accumulate the bill with compound assignment using relational comparisons.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer units.

Output Format:
Print one line: the bill amount to exactly 2 decimals.

Constraints:
0 <= units <= 5000.

questions.title: Set Bits and Highest Position
questions.description:
A debugging toolbox inspects the bits of a number. For the given non-negative integer report how many bits are set, the position of the highest set bit (0-indexed; use -1 when the number is 0), and whether the number is an exact power of two. Use the unsigned right shift >>> to walk the bits.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer n.

Output Format:
Three lines: 'Set bits: X', then 'Highest position: Y', then 'Power of two: Z' where Z is lowercase true or false.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000.

questions.title: Salary Bonus With Nested Ternaries
questions.description:
A company pays an annual bonus decided by rating and service years, coded as one nested ternary expression (if statements are forbidden): rating 1 earns 20 percent for 5 or more years of service, otherwise 15 percent; rating 2 earns 12 percent for 5 or more years, otherwise 8 percent; rating 3 always earns 5 percent. Also report the truncated whole-rupee monthly hike.

Input Format:
One line: salary (decimal number), years (integer) and rating (1 to 3), space separated.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Bonus: X' with X to exactly 2 decimals. Line 2: 'New salary: Y' with Y to exactly 2 decimals. Line 3: 'Monthly hike: N' where N is (int) (bonus / 12).

Constraints:
1000 <= salary <= 1000000; 0 <= years <= 40; rating is 1, 2 or 3.

questions.title: Decimal to Binary via Shifts
questions.description:
A low-level tool shows a number in base 2 without using Integer.toBinaryString: it starts from a single 1-bit flag shifted left until it sits above the highest set bit, then walks the flag down while printing one bit at a time. It also previews two shift results.

Input Format:
One line with a single integer n.

Output Format:
Line 1: 'Binary: B' with no leading zeros (just 0 when n is 0). Line 2: 'Doubled: X' which is n << 1. Line 3: 'Halved: Y' which is n >> 1.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 1000000000.

questions.title: Fast Power Modulo Calculator
questions.description:
Cryptographic routines raise huge powers but only need the remainder. Compute base raised to exponent modulo m using fast modular exponentiation (square-and-multiply) in a while loop. Remember that in Java the * operator binds tighter than %, so result * base % m means (result * base) % m.

Input Format:
One line with three space-separated integers: base, exponent and modulus.

Output Format:
Print one line: base raised to exponent, modulo modulus.

Constraints:
1 <= base <= 2000000000; 0 <= exponent <= 1000000000; 1 <= modulus <= 2000000000.
